summary_html: An intake **screen** is elevated to a formal **investigation/assessment** under state criteria. CAPTA and CFSR establish the federal expectations for screening, timelines, and investigative quality.
authority_html:

- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal performance/quality review framework

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.holding: The court held that a finding of abuse under the physical-injury definition of RSA 169-C:3 requires a determination that the act was committed under circumstances indicating harm or threatened harm to the child's life, health or welfare, and reversed the agency's fair hearing finding of abuse based on two minor, isolated incidents.
key_cases.relevance: The opinion sets out how a report moves from intake to investigation and to a probable cause determination, and what the agency must ultimately prove.
key_cases.quote: On such a record, in a case where difficult lines between corporal punishment and child abuse must be drawn, we hold that the findings of abuse must be reversed

key_cases.holding: The court held that when the division finds a report of abuse or neglect 'founded' and records that determination in the central registry it adjudicates the subject's status and must, under Part I, Article 15 of the State Constitution, give written notice of the determination, its reasons, the identification of the named perpetrator, and the rights of access and administrative challenge; the division's notice here was constitutionally inadequate.
key_cases.relevance: When intake escalates to an investigation that concludes in a 'founded' determination, the court requires notice of the determination and of the right to be heard before the record is maintained.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the notification procedures employed by the division did not afford the Bagleys the protections required by part I, article 15 of the New Hampshire Constitution

state_agency.hotline: 1-800-894-5533 (in-state only) or 603-271-6562; DCYF Central Intake is staffed 24 hours a day, including weekends and holidays

mandatory_reporters: Any person (universal mandatory reporting) — N.H. Rev. Stat. Ann. § 169-C:29
Physicians, surgeons, county medical examiners, psychiatrists, residents, interns
Registered nurses and hospital personnel (admission, examination, care and treatment)
Teachers, school officials, school nurses, school counselors
Social workers, day care workers, and any other child or foster care workers
reporting_details: New Hampshire is a universal-reporter state: RSA 169-C:29 lists physicians, dentists, psychologists, registered nurses and hospital personnel, teachers, school officials and school nurses, social workers, day care and other child or foster care workers, law enforcement officials and clergy, and closes with “any other person having reason to suspect that a child has been abused or neglected,” all of whom “shall report the same in accordance with this chapter.” RSA 169-C:30 sets the route and the form: an oral report “shall be made immediately by telephone or otherwise, and followed within 48 hours by a report in writing, if so requested, to the department” — the Department of Health and Human Services, which takes reports through the DCYF Central Intake Unit at 603-271-6562 or 1-800-894-5533 (in-state only), staffed 24 hours a day including weekends and holidays.
